title: Anne Hathaway Credits Rihanna, Says She’s Learned to “Chill Out” in Her Career Style Evolution
body:
Anne Hathaway used her recent appearance on a national morning show to reflect on a whirlwind year that saw her headline five films, debut a new thriller, and navigate motherhood with a style evolution she credits to pop icon Rihanna. Speaking with co‑host Gayle King, the Oscar‑winning actress revealed how the demands of back‑to‑back projects forced her to “chill out” and re‑evaluate the way she approaches both work and personal life, while also sharing the inspiration behind her now‑famous maternity look.

The conversation centered on Hathaway’s upcoming psychological thriller “Verity,” a departure from the period dramas and rom‑coms that have defined much of her career. In “Verity,” she portrays a writer entangled in a dark, metafictional mystery, a role that required intensive preparation and a grueling shooting schedule. “I had no idea I’d end up in five movies this year,” Hathaway admitted, noting that the relentless pace left little room for the perfectionism that once dominated her process. “I learned to trust the moment, to let things unfold without over‑analyzing every choice.” That mindset shift, she explained, has become a guiding principle for future projects, allowing her to balance artistic ambition with mental well‑being.

Beyond the set, Hathaway’s transformation into motherhood has been equally public. The actress, who welcomed her first child earlier this year, has been praised for a bold, street‑style maternity wardrobe that blends high fashion with comfort. When asked about the source of her sartorial confidence, she smiled and pointed to Rihanna’s own fearless approach to fashion. “Rihanna showed me that you can be unapologetically you, even when you’re pregnant,” Hathaway said. “She turned the idea of maternity wear on its head, and I wanted to do the same—mixing luxe fabrics with sneakers, oversized jackets with delicate dresses.” The resulting aesthetic has sparked a wave of copycat looks on social media, highlighting a broader cultural shift toward more relaxed, expressive maternity fashion.

Industry insiders note that Hathaway’s candidness about “chilling out” signals a larger trend among A‑list talent who are pushing back against the relentless perfectionism that Hollywood often demands. Actors such as Jennifer Lawrence and Adam Driver have spoken publicly about the mental toll of constant scrutiny, prompting studios to reconsider scheduling practices and support systems. Hathaway’s admission that she is learning to “let go” may encourage peers to prioritize mental health without fearing career repercussions. Moreover, her willingness to discuss style influences from outside the traditional Hollywood sphere underscores the growing cross‑industry dialogue between music, fashion, and film.

The impact of Rihanna’s influence extends beyond personal style; it reflects the increasingly porous boundaries between entertainment sectors. Rihanna’s own venture into fashion with her luxury brand has already reshaped red‑carpet expectations, and Hathaway’s acknowledgment of that inspiration demonstrates how musicians are now key arbiters of style for actors. This convergence is further evidenced by recent collaborations, such as Beyoncé’s involvement in film soundtracks and Pharrell Williams’ production work on major motion pictures, suggesting a future where creative cross‑pollination becomes the norm rather than the exception.

Looking ahead, Hathaway’s upcoming projects, including “Verity” and a slated period piece set in the 1920s, will test whether her newly adopted relaxed mindset can sustain the intensity of varied roles. Fans and critics alike will watch to see if this philosophical shift translates into nuanced performances that balance vulnerability with the confidence she now exudes off‑screen. As the entertainment landscape continues to evolve, Hathaway’s blend of professional adaptability and personal authenticity may well serve as a blueprint for other artists navigating the pressures of fame, family, and fashion.
